proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (>2 eV) electronic insulator that is chemically compatible with both sulfide electrolytes and oxide cathodes, and it is a standard protective coating for LiCoO2 in sulfide all-solid-state cells. Li3AlF6 is a wide-gap halide insulator. Fluorides with strongly ionic Al-F and Li-F bonds should be far less reactive toward the sulfide electrolyte than oxides. The earlier Li3PO4 contact released P2O5, SO2 and SCl4, which points to oxide-sulfide redox and metathesis as the main penalty. A fluoride should avoid that pathway, and LiCoO2 is also a standard fluoride-coated cathode system.
